Stone rubbing dated 1903? Original stone was engraved in Fuchang 7 nian, i.e. 1136 A.D. The stone is now in the Forest of Stone Steles Museum in Xi'an, China. Covers China in Nan Song Dynasty, from east to the sea, including Korea to the west of Pamier area, from north to the Great Wall, northeast to Heilongjiang region, to the south of Hainan Island. Shows mountains, rivers, lakes, and more than 400 administrative place names of China. Typewritten on paper slip affixed in lower margin of original map: Bulletin de l'Ecole Française 1903, Hanoi, F.H. Schneider. On bottom of map: Carte A. Includes text. LC copy accompanied by negative photocopy. Available also through the Library of Congress Web site as a raster image.
